title: Time: Analogue and Digital Clocks, Calendars and Time Problems
seo_title: Grade 3 Time Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Time: tell 12-hour time in hours, half hours, quarter hours and minutes on analogue clocks and digital clocks; use calendars to calculate and describe lengths of time in days, weeks or months; calculate length of time and passing of time.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 3 maths worksheets: telling the time to the quarter hour and minute, a.m. and p.m., time facts and time problems. 100 questions with clocks and memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The short hand shows the hour; the long hand shows the minutes.
  • Each number on the clock is 5 minutes for the long hand.
  • 60 minutes = 1 hour; 24 hours = 1 day; 7 days = 1 week.
  • a.m. is before midday; p.m. is after midday.

Examples

Example

Long hand on 4, short hand just past 7

4 × 5 = 20

Answer: 20 past 7

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The handsThe short hand is the hour.
Counting in 1sCount in 5s for the numbers.
100 minutesAn hour is 60 minutes.

faq.a: Grade R to Grade 3 in South African schools. Grade 3 is the last year; learners are about 8 to 9 years old.

items.q: The digital clock shows a time. How do we say it?
items.e: 8:35 is 35 minutes past 8. That is more than half past, so say to the next hour. 60 − 35 = 25 minutes to 9: 25 to 9.

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The long minute hand points to 10. Count in 5s: 10 × 5 = 50 minutes past. That is 10 minutes before 9 o’clock (60 − 50 = 10). The minute hand is on the left-hand side, so we say to 9. It is 10 to 9.

The short hour hand is between 6 and 7, so the hour is still 6. The long minute hand points to 1. Count in 5s: 1 × 5 = 5 minutes past. The minute hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past 6. It is 5 past 6.

items.q: The digital clock shows a time. How do we say it?
items.e: 4:20 is 20 minutes after 4 o’clock. It is less than half past, so say past: 20 past 4.

The short hour hand is between II (2) and III (3), so the hour is still 2. The long minute hand points to VII (7). Count in 5s: 7 × 5 = 35 minutes past. That is 25 minutes before 3 o’clock (60 − 35 = 25). The minute hand is on the left-hand side, so we say to 3. It is 25 to 3.

items.q: The digital clock shows a time. How do we say it?
items.e: 2:50 is 50 minutes past 2. That is more than half past, so say to the next hour. 60 − 50 = 10 minutes to 3: 10 to 3.

The short hour hand is between 11 and 12, so the hour is still 11. The long minute hand points to 11. Count in 5s: 11 × 5 = 55 minutes past. That is 5 minutes before 12 o’clock (60 − 55 = 5). The minute hand is on the left-hand side, so we say to 12. It is 5 to 12.

items.q: The digital clock shows a time. How do we say it?
items.e: 11:40 is 40 minutes past 11. That is more than half past, so say to the next hour. 60 − 40 = 20 minutes to 12: 20 to 12.

items.e: Noon is 12 o’clock in the middle of the day. Midnight is 12 o’clock at night.

c: 12 o’clock in the middle of the day
items.e: Midnight is 12 o’clock at night, when one day ends and the next day starts.
am times go from midnight to noon (night and morning). pm times go from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening).
The afternoon is after noon, so it is a pm time. 2:30 am is in the middle of the night. So the answer is 2:30 pm.

items.q: Which is a sensible time for school to start?
items.e: School starts in the morning, so it is an am time. 3:50 am is the middle of the night. So the answer is 8:50 am.
Midnight is 12 o’clock at night. 11:50 pm is 10 minutes before midnight. 11:50 am is 10 minutes before noon. So the answer is 11:50 pm.

items.q: It is 11:30 am. What time will it be 1 hour later?
items.e: 1 hour after 11:30 is 12:30. It is now after noon, so it changes to pm: 12:30 pm. (12:30 am is just after midnight.)

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 3. Count in 5s to 15, then on in 1s: 19 minutes past. It is the morning, so it is am. So it is 7:19 am.

The short hour hand is between 3 and 4, so the hour is still 3. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 4. Count in 5s to 20, then on in 1s: 21 minutes past. It is after noon, so it is pm. So it is 3:21 pm.

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 6. Count in 5s to 30, then on in 1s: 31 minutes past. It is the morning, so it is am. So it is 8:31 am.

The short hour hand is between 12 and 1, so the hour is still 12. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 6. Count in 5s to 30, then on in 1s: 31 minutes past. It is after noon, so it is pm. So it is 12:31 pm.

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 5. Count in 5s to 25, then on in 1s: 26 minutes past. It is after noon, so it is pm. So it is 7:26 pm.

The short hour hand is between 5 and 6, so the hour is still 5. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 10. Count in 5s to 50, then on in 1s: 52 minutes past. It is after noon, so it is pm. So it is 5:52 pm.

items.q: Write 20 past 10 in the morning as a digital time.
items.e: “20 past 10” means 20 minutes after 10 o’clock: 10:20. It is in the morning, so it is am: 10:20 am.

items.q: Write 25 to 9 in the morning as a digital time.
items.e: “25 to 9” means 25 minutes before 9 o’clock. 60 − 25 = 35, so it is 35 minutes past 8: 8:35. It is in the morning, so it is am: 8:35 am. (Not 9:35 am: that is after 9 o’clock.)

items.q: Write 20 to 5 in the afternoon as a digital time.
items.e: “20 to 5” means 20 minutes before 5 o’clock. 60 − 20 = 40, so it is 40 minutes past 4: 4:40. It is in the afternoon, so it is pm: 4:40 pm. (Not 5:40 pm: that is after 5 o’clock.)

items.q: Write 5 to 8 in the evening as a digital time.
items.e: “5 to 8” means 5 minutes before 8 o’clock. 60 − 5 = 55, so it is 55 minutes past 7: 7:55. It is in the evening, so it is pm: 7:55 pm. (Not 8:55 pm: that is after 8 o’clock.)

items.q: On a 24-hour clock, what is 3 pm?
items.e: pm times are after noon. Add 12 to the hour: 3 + 12 = 15. So 3 pm is 15:00.

items.q: A 24-hour clock shows 18:30. What is this in 12-hour time?
items.e: Take away 12 from the hour: 18 − 12 = 6. It is in the evening, so it is 6:30 pm. (Do not just drop the 1: 18:30 is not 8:30.)

items.q: How is midnight shown on a 24-hour clock?
items.e: On a 24-hour clock a new day starts at midnight, so midnight is 00:00. 12:00 is noon.
There are 60 seconds in 1 minute.
There are 60 minutes in 1 hour. (Not 100: time does not count in hundreds.)
There are 24 hours in 1 day: 12 am hours and 12 pm hours. 12 + 12 = 24.
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday: 7 days. (5 is just the school days.)
January to December: 12 months. (52 is the number of weeks.)

items.q: How many days are in a year that is not a leap year?
items.e: A normal year has 365 days. A leap year has 1 more: 366.

items.q: How many days are in a leap year?
items.e: A leap year has 1 extra day, 29 February. 365 + 1 = 366 days.

items.q: How many days does February have in a normal year?
items.e: February is the shortest month. It has 28 days, and 29 days in a leap year. It never has 30.

items.q: In a leap year, how many days does February have?
items.e: In a leap year February gets 1 extra day: 28 + 1 = 29 days.
Remember: “30 days has September, April, June and November. All the rest have 31, except February.” So September has 30 days.

items.q: How many minutes are in half an hour?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30 minutes. (Not 50: an hour is not 100 minutes.)

items.q: How many minutes are in a quarter of an hour?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. A quarter of 60 is 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes. (25 would be a quarter of 100.)
1 minute = 60 seconds. 2 minutes = 60 + 60 = 120 seconds.
1 hour = 60 minutes. 2 hours = 60 + 60 = 120 minutes. (Not 200: an hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)
1 minute = 60 seconds. 60 + 30 = 90 seconds. (Not 130: a minute is 60 seconds, not 100.)
1 day = 24 hours. 2 days = 24 + 24 = 48 hours.

items.q: About how long does it take to brush your teeth?
items.e: 2 seconds is far too quick, and 2 hours is far too long. Brushing your teeth takes about 2 minutes.

items.q: About how long does a Grade 3 learner sleep at night?
items.e: Children sleep from the evening until the morning. That is about 10 hours.

items.q: Which unit would you use to time a 50 m race at the athletics day?
items.e: A 50 m race is over very quickly, in less than a minute. We time it in seconds.

items.q: About how long is a school day?
items.e: School starts in the morning and finishes in the afternoon. That is about 6 hours.

items.q: A TV programme starts at 4:10 pm and ends at 4:35 pm. How long is it?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 35 − 10 = 25 minutes.

items.q: Kabelo starts reading at 7:05 pm and stops at 7:45 pm. How long does he read for?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 45 − 5 = 40 minutes.

items.q: Morning break starts at 10:30 am and ends at 10:45 am. How long is break?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 45 − 30 = 15 minutes.

items.q: Zinhle’s piano lesson is from 5:20 pm to 5:50 pm. How long is the lesson?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 50 − 20 = 30 minutes.

items.q: Assembly starts at 9:05 am and ends at 9:27 am. How long is assembly?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 27 − 5 = 22 minutes.

items.q: A soccer match starts at 2:45 pm and ends at 3:30 pm. How long is the match?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 2:45 pm to 3:00 pm is 15 minutes. Then 3:00 pm to 3:30 pm is 30 minutes. 15 + 30 = 45 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: Ruan gets on the school bus at 8:40 am. He gets to school at 9:05 am. How long is the bus ride?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 8:40 am to 9:00 am is 20 minutes. Then 9:00 am to 9:05 am is 5 minutes. 20 + 5 = 25 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: Thandi’s swimming lesson is from 3:50 pm to 4:35 pm. How long is it?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 3:50 pm to 4:00 pm is 10 minutes. Then 4:00 pm to 4:35 pm is 35 minutes. 10 + 35 = 45 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: A cake goes in the oven at 11:48 am. It comes out at 12:13 pm. How long does it bake?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 11:48 am to 12:00 pm is 12 minutes. Then 12:00 pm to 12:13 pm is 13 minutes. 12 + 13 = 25 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: A film starts at 5:50 pm and ends at 7:20 pm. How long is the film?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 5:50 pm to 6:00 pm is 10 minutes. Then 6:00 pm to 7:20 pm is 1 hour 20 minutes. 10 + 80 = 90 minutes = 1 hour 30 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)
am times go from midnight to midday (night and morning). pm times go from midday to midnight (afternoon and evening).

items.q: The long minute hand goes all the way around the clock once. How much time has passed?
items.e: The minute hand passes all 60 small marks, one for each minute. 60 minutes = 1 hour. In that time the short hour hand moves from one number to the next.

The short hour hand is between 1 and 2, so the hour is still 1. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 3. Count in 5s to 15, then on in 1s: 17 minutes past. It is after midday, so it is pm. So it is 1:17 pm.

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 7. Count in 5s to 35, then on in 1s: 37 minutes past. It is the morning, so it is am. So it is 8:37 am.

items.q: Write quarter to 9 in the morning as a digital time.
items.e: “quarter to 9” means 15 minutes before 9 o’clock. 60 − 15 = 45, so it is 45 minutes past 8: 8:45. It is in the morning, so it is am: 8:45 am. (Not 9:45 am: that is after 9 o’clock.)

At 3:37 the long hand is 2 small marks past the 7 (count in 5s to 35, then on in 1s to 37), and the short hand is between 3 and 4. That is clock C. (Clock A shows 4:37; clock B shows 3:23; clock D shows 3:07.)

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 9. Count in 5s to 45, then on in 1s: 46 minutes past. It is after midday, so it is pm. So it is 7:46 pm.

items.q: Write 25 to 4 in the afternoon as a digital time.
items.e: “25 to 4” means 25 minutes before 4 o’clock. 60 − 25 = 35, so it is 35 minutes past 3: 3:35. It is in the afternoon, so it is pm: 3:35 pm. (Not 4:35 pm: that is after 4 o’clock.)

At 10:12 the long hand is 2 small marks past the 2 (count in 5s to 10, then on in 1s to 12), and the short hand is between 10 and 11. That is clock A. (Clock B shows 11:12; clock C shows 10:48; clock D shows 10:02.)

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 5. Count in 5s to 25, then on in 1s: 27 minutes past. It is the morning, so it is am. So it is 7:27 am.
